input.quote: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The § 12.1 grant is expressly "revocable" with no stated trigger, i.e. revocable at IBM's discretion, and names only Customer — Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are excluded, and § 14.17 confirms no other licences or rights are granted. That combination is walk-away territory under this rule and fails the fallback (no affiliate coverage even on written notice). Successor transfer is separately addressed in § 14.10, which permits assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition, so only the revocability and affiliate/contractor scope need fixing. Redline extends the grant to Affiliates and contractors and limits revocation to our uncured material breach.

proposal.summary: Extend Base Components licence to Affiliates and contractors and remove revocability at will
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the licence to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, since they operate the Services with us, and replaced the at-will revocability with revocation only for our uncured material breach. Our playbook does not accept a licence the vendor can revoke at its discretion; if helpful, we can cover Affiliates on written notice instead.

ops.oldText: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.
ops.newText: IBM grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on Customer's behalf a nonexclusive license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement, revocable only in the event of Customer's material breach that remains uncured following written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.
